best_candidate: Deep LDL-C lowering to guideline target with approved agents
why: it is the only mechanism with repeated randomised evidence at the mortality level, and the effect is quantitative and predictable rather than directional
quantitative_effect: 22% relative reduction in major vascular events per 1 mmol/L LDL-C reduction
second_choice: low-dose colchicine - the only anti-inflammatory with a positive outcome signal and a guideline place, and notably NOT an IL-6 inhibitor
what_the_repository_contributes: it rules things out: the combined architecture is not robust in its own model, the cell patch is below the LVEF surrogate threshold, and the inflammatory arm's marker has now been shown in 6,385 patients not to move outcomes when manipulated
this_is_not_a_cure: no candidate here is a cure. None reverses established coronary disease or restores infarcted myocardium. The best-supported option slows progression and reduces events; it does not undo the disease
